title: fix(plugin-approvals): the generic data door serves sys_approval_request rows by the approvals door's visibility (#22559)
body:
Fixes #22559
Clause-②: no

## What this does

A read of `sys_approval_request` through the generic data door (`find`, `findOne`, `count`, `aggregate` on the engine, so `GET /api/v1/data/sys_approval_request`, the by-id route, `POST .../query`, the export route, the MCP data tool and every other engine read) now returns only the requests the approvals door (`/api/v1/approvals/*`) serves the same caller. Before this, once a deployment granted read on the object, that door served every request of the organization, including the payload snapshots of records the caller cannot open. The default (no grant, `403`) is unchanged.

The rule is #8652's, applied as ruled: participants (submitter, current approver, past actor) and the override actor see a request; a reader of the record it is about sees it read-only, only on an object the deployment opted in (`recordReaderVisibleObjects`, default OFF). The declarative opt-in stays objectstack-ai/objectstack#22560's.

| file | change |
|---|---|
| `packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/request-read-gate.ts` | new: the read middleware on `sys_approval_request` |
| `packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approval-service.ts` | `visibleRequestIdsFor(context, target)`, the approvals door's own `visibleRequestIds` made reachable; `findRequestRow`, the one by-id row read `loadRequest` and the gate share; the record-reader tier never anchors on `sys_approval_request` itself |
| `packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approvals-plugin.ts` | binds the gate when the service runs; the option's doc names both doors |
| `packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/payload-predicate-guard.ts` | `pinnedSubjectObject` generalised to `pinnedEquality(where, column)`, the one pin reader both seams use; behaviour of the guard unchanged |
| `packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/sys-approval-request.object.ts` | comment only |
| `packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/request-read-gate.integration.test.ts` | new: the pins |
| `packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/payload-predicate-guard.test.ts` | fixture re-judged (below) |
| `.changeset/22559-approval-request-read-gate.md` | `patch` |

## Which definition the gate consumes, and why

**Hypothesis 1 held.** The one definition is `ApprovalService.visibleRequestIds`: `null` for the override actor (a system context included), otherwise the participant set with the default-OFF record-reader tier (`addRecordReaderVisibleIds`) applied strictly on top. It was private, so the service gains one public method, `visibleRequestIdsFor(context, target)`, which derives the organization the way `listRequests` / `loadRequest` do and calls it. The gate decides nothing itself: it reads which record the query names, asks the service, and ANDs an `id` constraint built from the ids the service returned. No second visibility rule exists.

**Hypothesis 2 held; I used the approvals door's tier, not `resolveReadableParentIds`.** That function lives in `plugin-audit` (`comment-access-hooks.ts`), is not exported from its index, and `plugin-approvals` does not depend on `plugin-audit` (the claim also excludes its source). The approvals door's tier already answers the same anchor the same way: one engine read of the record AS THE CALLER, so the record's own CRUD, sharing and RLS decide. Consuming it keeps one definition for both doors. Triage's "not the `sys_activity` shape" is pinned: switching the tier on for every object (ablation B) reddens exactly the tier-OFF reader pin.

**Hypothesis 3: measured, and the target is read off the query.** The data door's list arrives at the middleware with its filter already lowered into `ast.where`: implicit field filters (`?object_name=…&record_id=…`) and the filter-array spelling both arrive as conjunctive equalities, pinned in the tests through the real `ObjectStackProtocolImplementation.findData`. The gate maps the query to the approvals door's own read shapes:

- `object_name` and `record_id` both pinned (a record page's related list) is `listRequests({ object, recordId })`;
- `id` pinned (`GET /data/sys_approval_request/ID`) is a request loaded by id, which carries its own anchor (`loadRequest`); the row is read through the same `findRequestRow` `loadRequest` uses;
- anything else is untargeted, the participant set alone, as for the inbox. A pin under `$or` / `$not` names nothing, so it reads untargeted: narrower, never wider.

**Hypothesis 4 held.** Every read the service makes of `sys_approval_request` runs as the system, and the shared definition answers a system context `null` before any read, so the gate adds nothing to them and never re-enters itself through them. One re-entry path did exist: the tier's anchor read runs as the caller, so with the opt-in naming `sys_approval_request` itself it would pass through the gate, which asks about the row that one names, unbounded on a cycle (measured: worker out of memory, see ablation C). The tier now never anchors on `sys_approval_request`; a request is no business record.

**Hypothesis 5 held.** The override actor gets `null`, so Setup → Approvals → Requests for an administrator is unnarrowed (pinned: list, count and by id).

## How it composes with the attached-on-read `viewer` block (#22479)

`viewer` is attached by the approvals door only (`attachViewers`, on `listRequests` / `getRequest`). The gate decides which rows the data door serves; it never attaches `viewer`. So a row served on the data door carries no `viewer`, every decision action's `visible` predicate fails closed there, and a record reader the tier admits gets the row read-only on both doors: on the approvals door its `viewer` is `{ can_act: false, can_override: false, is_submitter: false }`. Both halves are pinned. The other seams on this object are unchanged and compose: the snapshot query guard refuses before the gate runs, and the snapshot redaction narrows what a served row's `payload_json` holds.

## Fail closed

- A failed visibility answer denies the read and logs one warning.
- A by-id read of a request the caller may not see answers exactly as a missing id does: `404 RECORD_NOT_FOUND` (the door's real answer, measured through `getData`). No existence oracle.
- A list's `total` and a grouped count are narrowed like its rows.
- A context-less programmatic call on a bare kernel is not narrowed, as for the sibling read seams; every real transport carries a context.
- The gate binds whenever the service runs, not behind `disableAutoHooks` (that switch is documented as the record lock's). An engine with no middleware seam gets one loud warning at boot.

## Tests and ablations

Rig: a real ObjectQL engine over better-sqlite3, the real `ApprovalsServicePlugin.start()` (so an unbound gate fails like an unwritten one), requests opened by the real `openNodeRequest`, and the real data-door normalizer. The one stand-in is record readability, one middleware on the business object. The subject resolves through `src/`: the test imports the plugin by relative path, so no `dist/` sits on its resolution path and the ablations needed no rebuild.

Pins (14): a non-participant who cannot read the record sees no request in a list, a record's list, a count or a grouped count; by id, a hidden request answers as a missing one; a reader of the record sees nothing while the tier is off; a participant sees their own requests and no one else's; control: an administrator and the system are unchanged; for every caller, the data door's ids equal the approvals door's, tier off and on; with the tier on, a reader of the record sees its request on a read naming the record (both spellings), read-only, and nothing on an untargeted read or on a record it cannot read; a failed answer denies; a request about a request never re-enters the gate.

Each ablation was committed-first, landed through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` (anchor hit counted, blob changed), and restored to the HEAD blob with `git diff HEAD` empty:

| ablation | mutation | result |
|---|---|---|
| A | gate unwired in `approvals-plugin.ts` | 10 failed / 4 passed. Red: the five tier-off negatives and parity, the three tier-on negatives and parity, both fail-closed pins. Green, as they should be: the administrator and system controls, the tier-on reader positive, the filter-array positive. First failure: `expected { ids: [ …(2) ], total: 2 } to deeply equal { ids: [], total: +0 }` |
| B | record-reader tier on for every object (the activity-stream shape) | 1 failed / 13 passed: `a reader of the record who participates in nothing sees nothing while the tier is off`, `expected { …(2) } to deeply equal { ids: [], total: +0 }`. Parity stays green, as it must: both doors loosen together |
| C | the self-anchor guard removed | with the fuse: 1 failed / 13 passed, `expected 9 to be 1` (re-entry depth). Without the fuse, the first run of this pin held the lock 7m56s and ended in a worker out-of-memory crash, which is why the pin reads depth through a fuse |
| D | the gate's catch made to fail open | 1 failed / 13 passed: `a visibility answer that fails denies the read, and says so` |

**Fixture re-judged.** `payload-predicate-guard.test.ts` queried the generic door as three readers who participated in no request and asserted they were served rows "as before". After this change they are served nothing, so 7 of its pins went red for a reason outside what that file measures. Its readers are now the requests' current approvers (pending-approver index rows), so the rows they query are rows they may read and the file still measures the snapshot guard alone; its refusal pins were green throughout.

## Verification (head `2a7dfed452`, which merges `origin/main` `d6c37919c7`)

- `pnpm turbo run build --filter='@objectstack/plugin-approvals...' --concurrency=1`: 32 tasks, exit 0.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-approvals exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2`: 65 files, **930 passed**, exit 0. The new file alone: 14 passed.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-approvals typecheck`: exit 0 (`tsc` build program, scripts program, and `check:test-typecheck`: the new test file adds no error; the ledger holds 8 files / 324 errors, unchanged).
- Lint, narrowed and proven: ESLint over the 7 changed `.ts` files, `--no-inline-config --format json`: 7 files, 0 errors, 0 warnings. Both new files are inside the linted population (`isPathIgnored` false, read from `eslint.config.mjs`), and the config enables no type-aware linting (no `parserOptions.project` / `projectService`), so this diff cannot move a verdict on an untouched file. The repo-wide `pnpm lint` is CI's.
- Declared to CI, not run here: the dogfood suites that boot the real stack with this plugin (`approval-snapshot-masked-field`, `approval-snapshot-credential-field`, `activity-text-predicate`, `audit-log-admin-search`). They resolve this package through `dist/`. Read through: their readers of `sys_approval_request` are its approvers (position holders), the platform administrator, or the system, so the gate admits each of them; the snapshot-guard refusals they pin happen before the gate runs.

## Gates

`node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` at `2a7dfed452` derives 67 commands; all 67 ran and answered **exit 0**, and `--ran` reconciles: `67 derived, 67 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN`. Two answered `3` (PREREQUISITE NOT MET) in that run and were re-run once their prerequisite was built: `pnpm check:i18n` (its build closure, all cached) and `pnpm check:dual-build-cjs-loads` (a full `turbo run build`, 72 tasks). On an earlier head `check-plugin-teardown-shape.mjs --self-test` answered `3` because its pinned fixture commit was outside the shallow clone; after `git fetch --unshallow origin main` it answers `0`. One went red on an earlier head and was fixed: `pnpm check:query-options-erasure` (the new test's engine options are now typed, not cast). The system-context census and the tenant-audit census are green with no regeneration: the gate reads no system flag of its own (the shared definition answers a system context), and the by-id row read moved into `findRequestRow` rather than being added.

## Acceptance notes

- **Same class, not fixed here (reported for filing):** `sys_approval_action` and `sys_approval_approver` declare `enable.apiMethods: ['get', 'list']` like `sys_approval_request`, and this package binds read middleware on `sys_approval_request` only. Under an app grant on either, the generic door is not narrowed to the approvals door's visibility (`listActions` gates through `loadRequest`). Not measured through HTTP here.
- `disableAutoHooks: true` also switches off the two snapshot seams on the generic door (the redaction and the predicate guard). This gate does not follow it. No production caller passes the option (`git grep`: tests only). Noted, not filed.
- `disableService: true` registers the five objects and binds no generic-door seam at all. Its one caller is `packages/cli/scripts/check-app-nav-i18n.mjs`, which reads navigation only. Noted, not filed.
- Cost: a non-administrator read of the object now pays the approvals door's participant probes (about four engine reads, plus the record read when the tier is on and a record is named), the same as one approvals-door list.
- The record-reader tier no longer anchors on `sys_approval_request` on the approvals door either. Only a deployment that names that object in the option sees a difference, and it is narrower.
- `origin/main` moved after the merge (`25be87612d`); not merged again, the PR's merge ref covers it.

## Seat's append: rework round 1 (head `a11d87ccaa`)

Appended by `domain:services` seat 1 (`session_013j5gkUCpqQiti4GgPqqmnt`) at 2026-10-10T03:41Z, from the dev's round-1 report (`6093383810` on #22559). Where the sentences above name `visibleRequestIdsFor`, or `findRequestRow` as a service member, **this section supersedes them**.

- **The published surface is unchanged.** The seat's round-0 review found that a new public `ApprovalService.visibleRequestIdsFor` widened the published class. It is gone.
  - The gate's visibility source is a module-scoped `WeakMap` that the `ApprovalService` constructor fills with an answer calling the class's own private `visibleRequestIds`.
  - The plugin reaches it through `requestVisibilitySourceOf(service)`, which `approval-service.ts` exports and `src/index.ts` does not re-export (`git diff origin/main -- packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/index.ts`: 0 bytes).
  - `findRequestRow` is a module function, the one by-id row read `loadRequest` and the gate share.
  - `ApprovalService`'s source member list equals `origin/main`'s (106 members). The built `dist/index.d.ts` carries no `visibleRequestIdsFor`, `requestVisibilitySourceOf` or `findRequestRow` (positive control: `listRequests(` 1).
- **Table row, `approval-service.ts`, superseded:** the gate's visibility source, in-package only (above); `findRequestRow`, a module function; the record-reader tier never anchors on `sys_approval_request` itself.
- **Merged with `origin/main` `99801d831f`** (merge `0522d7256e`, clean). That brings #22567 (the slotted `sys_approval_request` record page) and #22583, in regions disjoint from this PR's.
  - The page's highlights and details read the request through the data door by id, and the gate serves that read exactly when `getRequest` does.
  - Two by-id parity pins hold this: 6 callers × 2 requests, with the tier off and on, and a refused request answering `404 RECORD_NOT_FOUND`.
  - The page's Timeline tab reads `sys_approval_action`, which this PR does not gate. That is the sibling-tables card objectstack-ai/objectstack#22589.
- **Round-1 verification:**
  - The same 67 derived commands exit 0, and `--ran` reports 67 derived, 67 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED.
  - 66 files and 963 tests pass, and typecheck exits 0.
  - Ablation A (gate unwired) turns 12 of the suite's 16 pins red.
  - CI at `a11d87ccaa`: 31 success, 3 rostered skips.
- `Clause-②: no` stands. The surface is unchanged.
